For S ⊆ [k − 1], SCSP(S) without negation is approximation resistant if and only if (1) holds. The hardness claim, the “if” part, is currently proved only under the UGC, but our focus is on the algorithmic claim that the violation of (1) leads to an approximation algorithm that outperforms the best random assignment. Even though we were not formally able to prove Conjecture 1.1, we explain the rationale behind the conjecture and we prove it for the following two natural special cases in Section 2: 1.
